quest.name: The Road
quest.on_the_page: North out of Coldmere by the mill tracks on Rae's cart, the quiet road, chosen for his own: keep the company out of the writs' reach and the hunt's. A rider sent to bring the captain of the Ninth in alive, and not told why, has found him anyway, and at the river mill where Rae's salt goes a dozen carts stand drawn up the wrong way at the bridge, everyone looking back.

struggle: The weir: the rider down on the ice at his feet, her four riders held on the far bank only by the forms, his stick gone over the fall and his sword arm cut, and what she is to be is his to decide.
season: hard frost in the hill country north of Coldmere, the millpond iced over and every stone of the weir glazed with spray

recap: At the noon bell on the frozen weir, the rider's footwork met a man who would not move; she lies on the ice, and the choice is his.

story_so_far.darrow: With the last two fingers of his right hand slow for good, Darrow took the mill tracks north, let Rae decide for a river family, broke his word to tell Wren first once and kept it after, and answered an unsigned summons by the forms. On the frozen weir below the mill he chose one dry stone and stood on it against the finest footwork he had ever seen: moved once, cut once, he lost his stick to the fall and would not follow her off the stone, and she ran onto his point. On the ice she told him something about the ford that she did not understand.
story_so_far.hollis-garrow: Hollis moved the Captain's grip up the hilt and told him two lost fingers were an argument already over, gave a river boy the boot he carried down the mountain, and argued for answering the summons by the forms. He won, sulked about it, crossed the glazed weir on his backside to test his captain on the stone, told Wren she was for them, and kept his hands at his sides at noon because the forms said so.
story_so_far.wren-ashdown: Wren counted the Captain told-first twice and not-once, argued him away from the weir with arithmetic and lost, and kept a book on the morning that nobody would bet against. The night before, she told him she was frightened of keeping a column for him; the morning of it she offered him a lie, let it go, and counted for him that nobody on his own bank had ever asked him to kneel.
story_so_far.rae-thorne: Rae made the road lie with two carts out of one, took the call on a river family and carried them over the hill with her bell ringing, and told Darrow the sack's road before the mill. She read the weir for him, turned her cart broadside across its near end because oxen are allowed to stand, and brought him a sealed letter from the mill that was not hers to carry.
story_so_far.maelis-vorne: Maelis told him plainly what the frost had kept of his hand, warned the company what he would be taking onto the ice, and said a question could be answered by another mouth. At noon she waited on the bank with her needle threaded.
story_so_far.ash: Ash saw the rider on the skyline first and made no sound, watched the alders long after the meadow was empty, and tried to follow Darrow out onto the weir until Wren sat on her.
story_so_far.ysra-tal: Sent from Calden to bring in the captain of the Ninth alive and not told why, Ysra Tal lost a day to the carter's lying road, watched the company from a distance, and summoned him under the forms to the weir. Her one question was why he would not kneel. At the noon bell her footwork found a man who would not move, and she went down on the ice with his point in her shoulder, wanting a reason for the first time.

options: Spare her where she lies: have Maelis bind what the ice and the post have done, and let her men carry her off.
Break her blade hand on the ice and leave her for her men, and take the north road tonight while the hunt has no head.
Let her up with a message for the man who sent her, in Darrow's own words: the ford as he saw it from the water. Then watch her walk to her horse.
